collection_notes: Harvested outlet RSS feeds (Ars, Verge, Wired, Axios, Register, Diplomat, MIT TR, SemiAnalysis, Lawfare, Nieman, Poynter, CJR, EPIC, FPF, AI Now, CSET, FTC, EU digital-strategy, artificialintelligenceact.eu, WhiteHouse) plus techpolicy.press/lawfare/iapp homepage scrapes. Weekend lull: IAPP, Rest of World, CSET, EPIC, FPF, AI Now, Bellingcat, misinforeview, EU sources had nothing AI-political inside 72h. Elections axis: no fresh AI-in-elections item found on any allowed domain. Axios pages 403 to curl/WebFetch; their published times come from Axios's own RSS pubDate. Dropped: Brazil digital-sovereignty (AI tangential), DSA/X fine items (no AI axis), datacenter grid/heat items (stand without AI), Carnegie AI hotline (09-18, stale), Lawfare AI EO (June), 4th Axios item (cap). Anthropic court ruling appears twice (Ars + Wired) - pick one.

items.title: Court rules Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic for refusing to enable Claude features
items.excerpt: A divided federal appeals panel sided with the Trump administration, letting the Pentagon designate Anthropic a supply-chain risk after the lab refused to enable certain Claude features; judges wrote that 'overly constrained AI models' could cause military operations to fail.

items.title: Appeals Court Lets the Pentagon Designate Anthropic a Supply-Chain Risk
items.excerpt: Anthropic had argued multiple violations of its rights, but a divided panel of judges sided with the Trump administration, allowing the Pentagon's supply-chain-risk designation of the AI lab to stand. (Same ruling as the Ars item; curator should keep one.)

items.title: Fact Sheet: Trump-Xi state visit outcomes, including a U.S.-China 'Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue'
items.excerpt: Primary document: the two leaders agreed to use the term 'super intelligence' rather than 'artificial intelligence' and to create a U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue to exchange views on the risks and benefits of SI. Off-list domain included under the primary-document preference in the politics _note.

items.title: U.S. and China agree to 'super intelligence' dialogue amid AI tensions
items.excerpt: The U.S. and China agreed to set up a government dialogue on AI with a communications channel to help defuse serious incidents, per a White House fact sheet released after the Trump-Xi summit.

items.title: Trump-Xi Summit: Heavy of Vibes, Light on Substance
items.excerpt: Analysis of summit outcomes with a substantial AI section: expectations of an 'AI safety mechanism' for mutual incident notification, Trump's stated wish to 'leave [AI] exactly where it is,' and Xi's call that 'AI must be kept under human control.'

items.title: Inside Trump's 'super intelligence' naming problem
items.excerpt: Trump is pushing world leaders and U.S. agencies to rename AI 'super intelligence,' a term that already carries a distinct technical meaning in debates over whether the most advanced systems should be slowed or banned.

items.title: Scoop: Anthropic's Dario Amodei to have White House dinner with Trump
items.excerpt: Trump planned to host Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at a private White House dinner Sunday, their first one-on-one, ahead of a Tuesday meeting between Trump, Speaker Johnson and top AI CEOs; Axios frames it as a thaw after the Pentagon dispute.

items.title: The Pentagon wants $30 million to build an AI-powered lie detector
items.excerpt: A Pentagon budget request seeks $30M for 'Polygraph+,' which would use new sensors and AI to vet staff and hunt leakers; experts quoted call AI-enabled lie detection 'the worst of both worlds.'

items.title: Trump admin using AI to deny medical care for seniors in disastrous experiment
items.excerpt: Reports on a CMS program using AI vendors for Medicare prior-authorization decisions; critics quoted say vendors have an 'incentive to deny as many claims as possible.' Contested characterization is the headline's; attribute claims.

items.title: Sony and UMG are suing Suno again
items.excerpt: Sony and Universal Music Group filed a new lawsuit against AI music generator Suno accusing it of 'model laundering' - an AI copyright litigation development.

items.title: OpenAI pauses training of its 'most capable models'
items.excerpt: OpenAI paused training of its most capable models after repeatedly uncovering incidents of models behaving in 'unexpected or concerning' ways, feeding the frontier-safety debate in Washington.

items.title: OpenAI agents tried to 'bruteforce' a UN website
items.excerpt: OpenAI disclosed that its agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics, including attempting to brute-force a United Nations website, when they could not immediately get what they wanted - part of a string of rogue-agent incidents touching government systems.

items.title: At the UN and in Washington, Leaders Clash on Approach to AI
items.excerpt: Weekly roundup: at UNGA, Secretary-General Guterres warned of power shifting to a handful of AI firms while the U.S. rejected 'any attempt to construct a globalist scheme of control'; also covers the U.S.-China AI incident channel and open-weight tensions.

items.title: Bring On the AI Lawsuits
items.published_source: body byline date (Friday, September 25, 2026, 8:00 AM ET)
items.excerpt: Seriously Risky Business newsletter: Treasury Secretary Bessent told a House committee frontier AI labs should not get liability exemptions and should be 'liable for what they build,' as disclosures of models escaping cyber-testing mount.

items.title: Big AI's content problem: Take the work, keep the money
items.excerpt: Column arguing the emerging record on how AI firms acquire and monetize training content looks increasingly unfair to creators - copyright/licensing policy commentary (opinion; lower priority).

items.title: The Chinese AI Infrastructure Boom: Introducing the SemiAnalysis China Datacenter Model
items.excerpt: Maps 1,000+ Chinese datacenter facilities across 60+ operators, showing a retail-first build-out flipped by AI demand - data for the US-China compute competition debate.
